data.title: Fed policymakers concerned about financial system risks, minutes show
data.description:
Key points:
  • Minutes from Fed's October meeting showed expansive talk on financial stability risks
  • Fed officials discussed strategies to manage financial trouble

By Michael S. Derby

Financial stability risks tied to aggressive artificial intelligence investment and elevated asset prices are on the US central bank's radar, the minutes from the Federal Reserve's policy meeting last month showed on Wednesday.

The concern was raised as part of a broad review of financial risks by Fed policymakers and central bank staff at the October 27-28 policy meeting. That gathering saw officials hold interest rates steady despite ongoing worries about high and persistent levels of inflation. However, "almost all" policymakers agreed that further hikes would be needed if the economy evolved as they expected, the minutes showed.

"The staff judged that current vulnerabilities could amplify shocks somewhat more than usual, with elevated asset valuations and leverage at hedge funds representing the most salient vulnerabilities, while strong bank and household balance sheets provided an important buffer against more severe outcomes," the minutes said.

Policymakers expressed concern that huge levels of investment in AI technology could lead to trouble and create broader problems for both the financial system and economy.

"Almost all participants commented on risks associated with a scenario in which the returns on AI investment turned out to be disappointing to investors," the minutes said. "Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures," while "a few" of the unnamed Fed officials were concerned that AI exposure was being concentrated in a "small number" of companies.

Fed officials also cast an anxious eye toward hedge funds.

"Most participants highlighted hedge fund leverage or limited dealer intermediation capacity as potential channels of amplification during periods of market stress," the minutes said.

Fed staff described the financial system as "resilient," with banks having ample access to cash, according to the minutes. But some policymakers worried that "banking system vulnerabilities could emerge rapidly even after seemingly reassuring initial assessments."

Some were also worried the Fed's data on the banking system may miss the full range of exposure some financial firms have.

BUILDING RESILIENCE

Financial markets have been under stress in recent weeks amid questions about the future of AI and how the buildout of the technology has increasingly come to rely on debt. Past periods of financial trouble have been frequently associated with excessive borrowing, and some of those crises have driven the Fed to intervene to stabilize markets.

The latest minutes also showed Fed officials weighing how they can respond to future troubles.

"A few" policymakers mulled boosting banks' capital levels while some also said it is important to better prepare banks to use the Fed's emergency lending discount window facility, which is something officials have been working on for some time.

In addition, "a few" policymakers considered a novel strategy in which the Fed would set up a dedicated method of asset-buying that would explicitly target financial stability concerns.

The Fed is weighing the future of how it uses its balance sheet as a policy tool. Fed holdings have swollen massively over the last two decades due to huge bond purchases during the 2008 global financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic.

The pandemic experience has loomed particularly large because bond-buying that began in March 2020 started out as a stabilization tool that morphed into outright stimulus.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack is among those who would like to see a more clearly defined system for buying bonds that would also entail a strategy to sell them when a crisis has passed. Hammack said earlier this week that any program "should also be temporary, and holdings should be sold in a timely way once market financial stability is restored."

The minutes noted that "several" policymakers cautioned that monetary policy is not the right tool to deal with market trouble. But the large role now played by AI and technology investment in driving economic growth might complicate that view if large-scale problems emerged.

data.title: GTA 6 launch crash? Oddsmakers call it a toss-up
data.description:
Oddsmakers are calling a Grand Theft Auto 6 server outage a coin flip ahead of its Thursday launch.

Betting marketplace BetOline is asking whether PlayStation, Xbox, or Rockstar will go down on Thursday, listing both "yes" and "no" at dead-even -120 odds.

The toss-up pricing comes as PlayStation Network is already faltering hours before the game unlocks at midnight in the U.S. Outage tracker Downdetector has logged thousands of complaints—mostly login failures and connection errors—with reports climbing sharply Wednesday after noon to nearly 1,800 at the time of writing.

While U.S. gamers are still waiting, rolling midnight releases have already brought players online in countries such as Australia and New Zealand.

To ease the strain on their networks, Sony and Microsoft have both urged players to pre-download the roughly 212-gigbyte file ahead of time.

Early reviews of Grand Theft Auto 6 are strong, with IGN calling it "unprecedented, unbelievable, and unmissable," while Vice said it is Rockstar Games' "Magnus Opus," sending Take-Two Interactive Software stock surging roughly 7%.

The Metacritic score for the game is currently at 99 out of 100, which matches the highest score of all time. A recent estimate puts Grand Theft Auto 6 close to 15M digital preorders ahead of launch.

data.title: Oil Prices Fall Amid Supply Surplus Expectations, Middle East Tensions — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Farhan Rafid

Oil futures prices fell Wednesday as traders assessed the prospect of a global supply surplus amid renewed tensions in the Middle East and continued threats to regional oil shipments.

Front-month Brent crude futures settled down 1.3% at $91.95 a barrel, while front-month West Texas Intermediate crude fell 3.2% to $83.26 a barrel.

Analysts at ING said rising OPEC+ output, resilient Russian exports and growing U.S. inventories pointed to improving supply conditions, even as disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz remained a risk.

The analysts expect the global oil balance to loosen as production recovers, limiting the potential for a sustained rebound in prices.

The decline in U.S. crude futures was further fueled by the U.S. Energy Information Administration's weekly inventory report showing a bigger-than-expected 3.4 million barrel build in commercial crude oil stocks, a 5.2 million barrel increase in gasoline stocks, and a 1.6 million barrel rise in distillate stocks.

"Although the distillate supply gain was much smaller, the deficit narrowed to less than 8 million barrels in approaching a supply capable of meeting the needs of a cold winter should this trend be sustained," trading advisory firm Ritterbusch & Associates said in a note.

Analysts at ANZ Research said recovering Middle Eastern production was improving global oil availability, but warned that the increasing reliance on alternative export routes exposed shipments to further disruptions.

Although increased flows can limit price gains, global crude stockpiles at decade lows leave the market with a thinner buffer against fresh supply disruptions, Thadeu Dos Santos, an analyst at online trading provider Infinox said in a note Tuesday.

Abu Dhabi's ADNOC Logistics & Services, a subsidiary of state oil giant Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, said Wednesday that one of its vessels was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday evening, leaving one crew member missing and 11 injured. The company said the remaining crew members had been evacuated and that search-and-rescue operations were continuing.

Security risks remain elevated across the region. U.K. Maritime Trade Operations said a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz was struck for a second time near Oman's Khasab, causing a fire on board. The vessel had initially been struck Monday, leaving it disabled after an engine-room fire.

Meanwhile, UKMTO reported an attempted boarding of a cargo vessel southwest of Al Mukalla, Yemen, on Tuesday.

The latest incidents come amid renewed military exchanges between the U.S. and Iran, including attacks targeting American military facilities in Bahrain and a U.S. strike on an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz.

Write to Farhan Rafid at farhan.rafid@wsj.com and Anthony Harrup at anthony.harrup@wsj.com

data.title: Newsmax sues Fox to unwind $22 billion Roku takeover
data.description:
News outlet Newsmax sued Fox on Wednesday to block its $22 billion takeover of Roku, alleging the deal hurts competition in the fast-growing market for free, ad-supported television.

Here are more details:

  • Fox announced on November 6 that it had completed the acquisition, earlier than the companies had publicly projected after months of regulatory scrutiny, as per the lawsuit

  • The complaint, filed in the US District Court for the Northern District of California, asks the judge to halt Fox's integration of Roku and unwind the deal unless Fox sells either Tubi or The Roku Channel

  • Newsmax said the combination of Fox with Roku would give the company more than a 70% share of the free ad-supported streaming TV market

  • Roku did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment, while Fox said that the lawsuit was "wholly without merit."

  • "Upon closing, we commenced actively integrating this approved transaction for the benefit of consumers, partners and other stakeholders," Fox said in an email response to Reuters.

  • Newsmax says Fox's pledges to the Justice Department, including to not discriminate against non-Fox content in search results, are unenforceable because they were not set out in a consent decree or court order

  • Newsmax, which operates Newsmax TV and the Newsmax2 streaming channel, said it relies on The Roku Channel for distribution and that Fox had previously refused to carry Newsmax on Tubi

  • Last year, Newsmax filed a lawsuit in Wisconsin accusing Fox of suppressing competition in the market for conservative-leaning pay TV, after a US judge in Florida dismissed an earlier version of the case on technical grounds

  • The case was moved back to Florida earlier this year

data.title: UAE Court orders freeze on crypto tokens stolen from Binance wallets
data.description:
Key points:
  • Largest crypto heist on record attributed to North Korea
  • Binance says it will keep trying to recover stolen assets
  • Circle and World Liberty Financial among companies affected

By Elizabeth Howcroft and Hannah Lang

An Abu Dhabi court has ordered several major cryptocurrency companies to freeze digital assets worth billions of dollars as part of efforts to recover some of the $6.3 billion in tokens stolen from wallets operated by Binance, according to court documents seen by Reuters.

The Abu Dhabi Global Market Court decision seeks to prevent the stolen crypto from being moved and applies to companies including Circle and World Liberty Financial.

The court said the 18 named companies were not accused of wrongdoing. Many companies have already frozen tokens that were stolen from Binance on October 29 in the largest crypto heist on record. US authorities have attributed the attack to North Korea.

“We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers,” Dugan Bliss, deputy general counsel at Binance, said in a statement on Wednesday.

The Abu Dhabi Global Market financial center serves as Binance's global hub, and the company said the Financial Services Regulatory Authority there is its primary regulator.

Reuters was the first to report that Binance was granted a court order to aid asset recovery. Binance subsequently said in a blog post on Wednesday that, while it had absorbed the financial impact of the stolen funds and made customers whole, it had a responsibility to pursue the stolen assets and support law enforcement.

Binance has previously said that around $2.85 billion worth of the stolen crypto tokens had been frozen or intercepted by third parties. That includes Circle, which operates the stablecoin USDC, and World Liberty Financial, the crypto venture operated by US President Donald Trump's family, which has a stablecoin called USD1. Both tokens are pegged to the US dollar.

Under the court order, those firms and 16 others are required to maintain the freeze on the tokens involved in the heist, pending further court proceedings. They are also barred from lending, swapping or mixing the tokens with other assets.

El Salvador-based Tether, which issues the USDT token and previously said it had frozen $1.5 billion worth of the stolen funds, was not included in the court order. Bliss said Binance was working with Tether directly on the return of the frozen assets.

"In consultation with the relevant authorities, we will work directly with Binance in respect of reissuing the tokens," a spokesperson for Tether said.

Binance has hired US law firm Gibson Dunn as part of its efforts to recover the stolen crypto. In a statement, a lawyer from Gibson Dunn representing Binance called the injunction "one of, if not the, largest publicly known freezing orders ever made."

A further hearing is scheduled for December 1, when the court will consider whether the proprietary injunction — a freezing order that applies to claimed assets — should continue and on what terms.

David Wachsman, spokesman for World Liberty Financial, said: "As the security incident unfolded in real time, World Liberty received an alert from onchain data identifying the issue. We acted decisively to protect our users and our partners."

Circle did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

data.title: US FDA approves Sanofi's genetic disorder drug
data.description:
The US FDA on Wednesday approved Sanofi's oral drug venglustat, making it the first treatment for a type of rare genetic condition that affects the brain and nervous system, the health regulator said.

The drug, branded as Infilbray, was approved for adults and children weighing at least 15 kilograms, or about 33 pounds, with type 3 Gaucher disease, a rare inherited disorder that causes fatty substances to build up in the body and brain.

The approval was based on a late-stage study of 43 patients aged 12 years and older whose symptoms outside the brain and nervous system had been stabilized with enzyme replacement therapy.

Patients who received Infilbray once daily for 52 weeks showed improvement on a combined measure of muscle control, coordination and cognitive function compared with those receiving enzyme replacement therapy every two weeks.

The most commonly reported side effects included gastrointestinal problems and effects on mood.

data.title: CBOT corn falls to multi-month lows on firm dollar, sagging crude oil
data.description:
Chicago Board of Trade corn futures fell on Wednesday, with the benchmark December contract hitting a 4-1/2-month low on strength in the dollar, which makes US grains less competitive globally, and declines in crude oil prices, traders said.

  • CBOT December corn ended down 11-1/4 cents, or 2.52%, at $4.35-1/2 per bushel after hitting $4.34-1/4, the contract's lowest since June 30.

  • CBOT March corn ended down 10-3/4 cents, or 2.34%, at $4.48-1/2 a bushel.

  • The greenback firmed on expectations for an interest rate hike next month, pressuring grains and other commodities including gold.

  • A 1% slide in crude oil futures added to bearish sentiment, given corn's role as a feedstock for ethanol fuel.

  • The US Energy Information Administration reported weekly production of corn-based ethanol in the week to November 13 at 1.126 million barrels per day, down 4,000 bpd from the previous week.

  • Weekly US ethanol stockpiles rose to 24.908 million barrels, up 563,000 barrels from the prior week and a two-month high.

  • Traders shrugged off support from firming domestic cash markets for corn. The US corn harvest is winding down, with 88% complete, and farmers have been reluctant to sell grain at current prices, prompting end-users in some areas to raise their basis bids.

  • Ahead of Thursday's weekly export sales report from the US Department of Agriculture, analysts expected the government to report net export sales of US corn in the week to November 12 at 1.2 million to 2 million metric tons.

data.title: Bankrupt Dish Wireless Strikes $525 Million Settlement Deal With American Tower — WSJ
data.description:
By Alexander Gladstone

Dish Wireless struck a $525 million settlement with American Tower and said it is negotiating with other tower owners who claim they are owed billions of dollars as a result of the bankrupt company's botched 5G network build-out.

Dish is working on similar settlements with other large creditors, including Charter Communications, which provided infrastructure and services the company used as it built out the 5G network, Dish said at a court hearing Wednesday.

In 2025, after coming under pressure from the Federal Communications Commission, which said the rollout was too slow, Dish parent EchoStar pivoted to selling its spectrum licenses to AT&T and SpaceX and then began winding down the network.

The settlement funds come from a $2.4 billion creditor trust established by the FCC using proceeds from AT&T's purchase of EchoStar's spectrum licenses. Dish said the agreement with American Tower will require the FCC to approve making the funds available by the end of the year.

Crown Castle, the tower owner with the largest creditor claim of roughly $3.5 billion, said at the court hearing that Dish hasn't reached out to discuss a possible settlement. A lawyer for Crown said it felt like the child eating alone at the school cafeteria.

Dish Wireless, the EchoStar subsidiary tasked with building the network, filed for bankruptcy in June along with Dish DBS, another EchoStar subsidiary that used the chapter 11 process to effectuate a restructuring plan with its financial creditors.

While EchoStar's bid to build a nationwide 5G competitor failed, the company ended up with deals to sell its spectrum licenses for tens of billions of dollars and stock, making it one of SpaceX's largest shareholders.

In bankruptcy, Dish has resolved disputes with bondholders, who said EchoStar had siphoned value away from them, and is seeking to address claims from telecom infrastructure providers like American Tower, Charter and Crown Castle, who said they were owed money after Dish shut down its 5G plans.

data.title: Treasuries Extend Upward Move Despite Interest Rate Concerns
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Treasuries have shown another move to the upside during trading on Wednesday, extending the advance seen over the two previous sessions.

Bond prices saw initial weakness but have climbed firmly into positive territory as the day has progressed. Subsequently, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, has fallen 3.5 basis points to 5.068 percent.

The ten-year yield has moved lower for the third straight day, pulling back further off its highest levels in a month.

The continued strength among treasuries comes despite concerns about the outlook for interest rates following recent comments from Federal Reserve officials.

In an interview with CNBC this morning, Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank might need to 'shock people' with a half-point rate hike amid persistently high inflation.

'I'm very, very concerned about inflation. It's kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out,' Waller told CNBC's Steve Liesman. 'If you really want to get it down, you've got to start taking more aggressive actions.'

Meanwhile, the minutes of the Federal Reserve's latest monetary policy seeming confirmed the central bank is likely to resume raising rates in the near future.

The Fed minutes said 'almost all participants' judged that further action to raise rates would likely be appropriate in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent objective.

'A couple of participants noted that an increase of more than 25 basis points could warrant consideration at the next meeting if incoming inflation data were unfavorable,' the Fed said.

The central bank also said a few participants observed that inflation could prove more persistent than anticipated, necessitating a shift to a more restrictive policy stance.

The Fed's next monetary policy meeting is scheduled for December 8-9, with CME Group's FedWatch Tool currently indicating a 94.7 percent chance of a quarter point rate hike.

data.title: Orlen, QatarEnergy in talks on new LNG deal days after contract termination, sources say
data.description:
By Marek Strzelecki

Poland's Orlen and QatarEnergy have begun talks on a new long-term liquefied natural gas supply deal days after the Polish group ended a decades-old contract, three people familiar with the matter said, potentially paving the way for a replacement agreement with more competitive pricing.

The discussions indicate Orlen's decision to exit the previous contract was aimed at improving terms rather than ending its relationship with QatarEnergy as a supplier.

Orlen said last week that "current market conditions offer alternative gas procurement options that are more favourable" than those available under the oil-linked deal signed in 2009.

The talks remain at an early stage and no agreement has been reached on volumes, duration, pricing or supply sources, the people said.

Orlen declined to comment. QatarEnergy did not respond to Reuters' request for comment.

One source said the parties had discussed a deal for around 1 million metric tons per annum (mtpa) of LNG, similar to the volume covered by the contract Orlen terminated last week, although the structure of any agreement remains under consideration.

Orlen wants additional gas supplies from QatarEnergy as part of a strategy to diversify its supplier base, a second source said.

The Polish company currently buys about 90% of its LNG from the US.

A third source said LNG sourced from the US was among the options under consideration, although discussions remain preliminary and no decisions have been made.

Market participants estimate the terminated contract was priced at around 16% of Brent crude. Analysts told Reuters last week that ending the agreement could save Orlen between $1.5 billion and $2 billion over the remaining term of the deal.

The second source said previous attempts to renegotiate the contract's pricing terms had failed, but terminating the deal could allow both sides to negotiate a replacement from a clean slate.

data.title: MP Materials moves higher as Needham resumes coverage with Buy rating
data.description:
MP Materials jumped 3.8% in Wednesday's trading as Needham resumed coverage with a Buy rating and $48 price target, believing it is in the early innings of a multi-year transformation from a legacy mining company into a vertically integrated rare earth materials and permanent magnet manufacturer capable of supporting key domestic customers.

The company has made steady progress over the past year building out its integrated platform and is expected to meet key milestones in materials and magnet production in H2 2026 and 2027, Needham analyst James Ricchiuti wrote, and with long-term support from the U.S. government as a 15% stakeholder and supply agreements with anchor customers GM and Apple, MP looks poised to become a major domestic permanent magnet supplier over the next three years.

MP is extending its heavy rare earth elements refining capability at the flagship Mountain Pass, California, integrated mining and refining facility—by far the biggest operation of its kind in North America—expanding processing output and magnet manufacturing at its Independence, Texas, facility supporting its GM supply deal, and has started construction on the new $1.25B 10X permanent magnet manufacturing plant in Northland, Texas, with commissioning planned for late 2028, Ricchiuti noted.

data.title: Wheat Leads Selloff in Grains — Daily Grain Highlights
data.description:
By Anthony Harrup

  • Wheat for December delivery fell 4.2% Wednesday on the Chicago Board of Trade to $5.70 a bushel, leading the market lower amid broad commodities selling.
  • Corn for December delivery fell 2.5% to $4.35 1/2 a bushel.
  • Soybeans for January delivery settled down 0.7% at 12.16 3/4 a bushel.

HIGHLIGHTS

Missing Catalysts: Grain futures are down and can't find reasons to rally. "We continue to look for something to grab hold of that will still be discussed tomorrow, but it's difficult to find it," Gary Sandlund of Futures International said in a note.

Overall commodity sentiment is in a state of deflation, he said, noting big drops in oil and gold "just to name a few." Geopolitical tensions seem to be the "new normal" and markets have adapted to it, Sandlund added.

Export Worries: The market is still wondering whether China will agree to buy U.S. corn when Presidents Trump and Xi Jinping meet. "Export demand remains a central focus for the corn market following its sluggish start to the marketing year," Matthew Lucas of Total Farm Marketing said in a note. "Adding to these concerns is the recent strength in the U.S. dollar index, which could further weigh on demand by making U.S. corn less competitive in the global market."

Off Track: Russia's wheat exports will likely fall to 2.7 million metric tons in November from October's 2.9 million tons as rail shipments slow, particularly to ports in Latvia and Lithuania, grains consultancy SovEcon said.

Rail shipments are among alternatives that Russia has used to export grain since Black Sea disruptions began in July. But "rail congestion and a shortage of grain railcars are slowing shipments," SovEcon said.

INSIGHT

Local Demand: Brazil's rapid ethanol expansion is providing corn growers with an alternative to export channels for surplus production, increasing competition for available corn and supporting local prices, Rabobank senior analyst Marcela Marini said in a note. Ethanol producers need continuous year-round flow of feedstock and have significant on-site storage capacity, which provides a stable outlet for corn production.

"The result is not an end to Brazil's exportable surplus, but a reduction in the volume that must be cleared through exports," Marini said. Export parity is still an important price reference, but is becoming less dominant.

Ethanol Output: U.S. ethanol stocks rose by 563,000 barrels last week to 24.9 million barrels, their highest level in two months, according to the Energy Information Administration. Production edged down to 1.126 million barrels a day from 1.13 million barrels a day the previous week, but was up from 1.091 million barrels a day a year earlier.

Production estimates among analysts surveyed by Dow Jones ranged from 1.095 million barrels a day to 1.15 million barrels a day. Inventory estimates ranged from 23.5 million barrels to 24.7 million barrels.

AHEAD

  • The USDA will release its weekly export sales report at 8:30 a.m. ET Thursday.
  • The USDA will release its monthly Cattle on Feed report at 3 p.m. ET Friday.
  • The USDA will release its weekly Grain Export Inspections report at 11 a.m. ET Monday.
  • The USDA will release its weekly Crop Progress report at 4 p.m. ET Monday.
